label: Trait category
summary: Whether the trait belongs to the given trait category.
details: It runs on a trait, not on a character. The game's categories are personality, education, childhood, commander, winter_commander, lifestyle, court_type, fame and health. Vanilla uses commander and personality most.

label: Trait has flag
summary: Whether the trait carries the given flag.
details: It runs on a trait itself, not on a character. Flags are labels set in the trait's definition, such as illness or can_not_marry. To ask the same about a character's traits, use has_trait_with_flag.

label: Trait rank
summary: Compares the rank of a trait the character has to a number, or to the rank of the same trait on another character.
details: Use either rank or character, one of them is enough. Not having the trait counts as rank 0, so a check like rank < 1 is also true for a character without the trait. Vanilla uses it mostly with wounded and the education traits.

fields.name: trait
fields.text: The trait (or trait group) whose rank is compared.

fields.name: rank
fields.values: a comparison with a number or script value, such as >= 2 or = 3

fields.name: character
fields.text: Another character whose rank in the same trait is compared against.
fields.values: a comparison with a character, such as > scope:heir

label: Has trait with flag
summary: Whether the character has at least one trait that carries the given flag.
details: Flags are labels set in a trait's definition, such as can_not_marry, is_immortal or commander_trait_flag. It saves listing every trait that has the flag. To check a single trait's own flag, use has_trait_flag.

label: Trait experience
summary: Compares how much experience (XP) the character has in a trait's level track to a value.
details: Some traits have several tracks; vanilla names the track for tourney_participant (for example foot or horse). For those you must name the track. For traits with a single track, leave it out. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=.

fields.name: trait
fields.text: The trait whose experience is checked.

fields.name: track
fields.text: Which experience track of the trait, only for traits that have more than one.
fields.values: a track key, such as foot or horse

fields.name: value
fields.text: The experience amount to compare against.
fields.values: a comparison with a number or script value, such as >= 50

label: Travel option
summary: Whether the travel plan has the given travel option active.
details: It runs on a travel plan (a character's journey). Vanilla uses it with options such as cultural_ambassador_option and leisurely_option.

label: Journey modifier
summary: Whether the travel plan currently has the given modifier.
details: It runs on a travel plan (a character's journey). Vanilla uses it with modifiers such as travel_guide_modifier and the pilgrimage modifiers.

label: Journey modifier time left
summary: Checks the time remaining on a modifier of the travel plan.
details: The game's documentation line is garbled (it quotes a county modifier example) and gives no usage, and vanilla does not use it, so the exact form is not known. It runs on a travel plan.

label: Has point of interest
summary: Whether the province has a travel point of interest of the given type.
details: The value is the key of a travel point of interest type, such as poi_buried_saint or poi_battles_historical.

label: Uses treasury
summary: Whether the character uses a treasury.
details: Write yes or no. The game's documentation does not say which characters have one; vanilla checks it in both directions.

label: Qualifies for legend seed
summary: Whether the character qualifies for the given triggered legend seed.
details: The value is the key of a triggered legend seed, such as king_arthur in the game's example. Vanilla uses it only with holy_warrior.

label: Has truce with
summary: Whether the character cannot attack the given character because of a truce.
details: Truces work in one direction: the check is about the scoped character being unable to attack the target, not the other way round. The target is another character, written as a scope or link.

label: Unit graphics
summary: Whether the culture uses the given set of unit graphics.
details: It runs on a culture. The value is a unit graphics key such as western_unit_gfx or mena_unit_gfx.

label: Has usable hook
summary: Whether the character has a hook on the given character that is not on cooldown.
details: A hook is leverage over someone. A hook that is on cooldown does not count. The value is the character the hook would be used on.

label: Custom coat of arms
summary: Whether the player has set a specific coat of arms for the title.
details: Write yes or no. It runs on a landed title. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Has valid casus belli
summary: Whether the war still has a valid casus belli (reason for war).
details: Write yes or no. The game says invalid casus belli are removed on the daily update, but one can still exist for a tick.

label: Has variable
summary: Whether the current scope has any of the named variables set.
details: A plain name checks one variable. A block with several name entries is true if at least one of those variables is set. The check runs on whatever the current scope is.

fields.name: name
fields.text: A variable to look for. Repeat the line to list several.

label: Has variable list
summary: Whether the current scope has the named variable list set.
details: The value is the name of the list. The check runs on whatever the current scope is.

label: Vassal stance
summary: Whether the vassal has the given vassal stance.
details: Vanilla uses stances such as courtly, zealot, parochial, belligerent and glory_hound. The game's documentation does not list the scope it runs on, but it speaks of the scoped vassal, so use it on a vassal character.

label: War result message
summary: Whether there is a war result message with the given outcome.
details: The outcome is victory, defeat, white_peace, invalidated or any. This is an interface trigger: it only works in certain places in the game's interface, not in ordinary script.

label: Has weak claim
summary: Whether the character has an explicit unpressed (weak) claim on the given title.
details: The game calls this an explicit claim; the counterpart for implicit claims is has_weak_implicit_claim_on. The value is a title.

label: Has weak hook
summary: Whether the character has a weak hook on the given character.
details: A strong hook does not count, only a weak one. The value is the character the hook would be used on.

label: Has implicit weak claim
summary: Whether the character has an implicit unpressed (weak) claim on the given title.
details: The game calls this an implicit claim; the counterpart for explicit claims is has_weak_claim_on. The game does not say how an implicit claim comes about. The value is a title. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Wrong holding type
summary: Whether the title is linked to a holding that its current holder or lessee cannot govern.
details: Write yes or no. It runs on a landed title.

label: Health
summary: Compares the character's health to a value.
details: The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla compares against named values such as poor_health, fine_health, good_health and death_chance_dying_health, or against plain numbers such as 2.5.

label: Heir resigns realm
summary: Whether the given character would give up their current realm titles back to their liege, instead of keeping them, when they inherit the title.
details: The example in the game is a cardinal who abdicates when elected Pope. It runs on a title, and the value is the character. A character who is not a ruler makes it fail. The character does not have to be in line for the title right now.

label: Herd
summary: Compares the herd of the domicile to a value.
details: The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla compares against named values such as max_herd and minor_herd_value. It also writes a block with value and multiply, for example { value = max_herd multiply = 0.9 }. The game does not document the block; it presumably scales the value (here, 90 percent of the maximum herd).

fields.name: value
fields.text: The base value to compare against, in the block form.
fields.values: a number, script value or named value such as max_herd

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: A factor that presumably scales that value in the block form.

label: Heresy threshold
summary: Compares the faith's heresy threshold to a value.
details: The threshold starts from a game default and doctrines can change it. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Highest title tier
summary: Compares the tier of the highest title the character holds to a tier.
details: Vanilla compares against tier_county, tier_duchy, tier_kingdom and tier_empire. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla also writes a block where value takes another character's tier and add or subtract shifts it by a number of tiers.

fields.name: value
fields.text: A tier taken from somewhere else, in the block form.
fields.values: a script value such as root.highest_held_title_tier

label: Highest skill
summary: Whether the given skill is the character's highest skill, not counting prowess.
details: It is also true when other skills have the same top value. Use martial, stewardship, diplomacy, intrigue or learning. To include prowess, use highest_skill_including_prowess.

label: Highest skill (with prowess)
summary: Whether the given skill is the character's highest skill, counting prowess too.
details: It is also true when other skills have the same top value. Vanilla uses it only with prowess.

label: Is landed
summary: Whether the character is landed, meaning they hold a county or barony.
details: Write yes or no. Vanilla uses it once.

label: Holy site artifact count
summary: Compares the number of artifacts in the holy site's inventory to a number.
details: The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=.

label: Has an enshrined artifact
summary: Whether the holy site has any artifact in its inventory.
details: Write yes or no.

label: Artifact in slot
summary: Whether the holy site has an artifact equipped in the named slot.
details: The value is the key of an artifact slot. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Holy sites controlled
summary: Compares how many holy sites the faith controls to a number.
details: The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla also writes a plain number, which means equals.

label: Max holy sites
summary: Compares the maximum number of regular holy sites that faiths of the religion can have to a number.
details: It runs on a religion. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Min holy sites
summary: Compares the minimum number of regular holy sites that faiths of the religion have to a number.
details: It runs on a religion. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Horde size
summary: Compares the size of the domicile's horde to a value.
details: If a horde is currently raised, it counts that one. If none is raised, it counts the horde that could be raised. The comparison can be <, <=, =, !=, > or >=. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Time as hostage
summary: Checks how long the character has been a hostage.
details: Write a block with days, months or years and a comparison, such as { years >= 4 }. Vanilla uses years only.

fields.name: days
fields.values: a comparison with a number, such as >= 30

fields.name: months
fields.values: a comparison with a number, such as >= 6

fields.name: years
fields.values: a comparison with a number, such as >= 4
